newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia precious metal/gem sales exceed 95/96 plans.
newsitem.headline: Russia precious metal/gem sales exceed 95/96 plans.

text.p: Russia's sales abroad of precious metals and diamonds in 1995 were 1.5 times the planned level of 4.6 trillion roubles, or 50 percent above the level, a senior source at Russia's Audit Chamber said on Friday.
The source also told Reuters that sales in 1996 were twice the planned level of 4.5-4.6 trillion roubles.
The Audit Chamber is an independent body that is responsible for checking how Russia's federal budget is fulfilled.
The annual budget sets out in rouble terms the amount of platinum, palladium, gold, rough diamonds and other precious metals and stones that Russia exports each year to bring income into the budget.
"Maybe these sales were by the Central Bank or were 'independent' sales," the source said.
When asked why the sales were above planned levels, he said, "Maybe it's because revenues from privatisation were less and they needed other sources of revenue."

He said the government could not have printed money to cover budget shortfalls because of its agreement with the International Monetary Fund, adding that he thought the extra exports were "indirectly related" to the IMF's conditions for its aid package to Russia.

The IMF has a $10 billion, three-year loan agreement with Russia that requires Moscow to adhere to certain fiscal conditions concerning tax collection, pension and wage arrears and structural reforms of the economy.
Metals analysts in London and Johannesburg have long believed that Russia has been selling platinum and palladium stockpiles to earn much-needed foreign currency.
